lines: - **one-closing-commit** Close with one commit after clearing old paths everywhere; then tag, merge, delete the branch. Read details/closing.md first.
- **outward-needs-po** Push, release and other outward actions need the PO's consent; a stage permission alone does not cover commit, merge or push.
note: Long file: the six steps in order; the closing commit holds only what Review and Retro changed in the repository (no copying of outside memory, no Retro file made up to fill it); the tag's message says what the Sprint achieved; the project's health is judged by scrum/ alone, usually only the README needs updating.

adds_to_target: Acceptance criteria and refinement points may be renegotiated with the PO, or with the Scrum Master within a written handover; write each change and its reason in chapter 4, Increment notes.
note: Goes into the goal-fixed long file.

line: - **new-work-registered** New work goes in the product log first; the PO decides if it joins the Sprint; the Sprint Goal stays, scope is renegotiable.
- **log-is-the-handoff** Keep a log's header current and write what matters into it before a session ends. Read details/handoff.md first.
where_else: The Now and Waiting for PO header fields and reading them first are in the sprint log template (lines 4-5).
note: Merged with design-log#24 (same rule for the design log). Long file keeps: a session that picks up reads the header first, then checks the recorded permission; no separate handoff documents; at a pause commit within the authorized scope only if permitted (otherwise keep changes uncommitted and record the status and where to resume); this does not waive the pre-Test freeze commit or the closing commit; stop at a complete point. design-log#24 adds: in a design, write the half-finished work into the chapter it belongs to before a session ends; Now and permission to enter a stage do not by themselves authorize committing, merging or pushing; commit only if the PO explicitly recorded commit permission for it.

lines: - **outside-blocker** [sm] When something outside the team blocks the work, tell the PO at once.
- **mid-sprint-release** A release ready mid-Sprint goes out with the PO's consent; the Sprint does not end.
note: The two rows of the old table, one line each.

line: - **read-the-goal** Before a stage decision, read the exact goal text from its table; if you cannot, stop. Read details/gates.md first.
note: The old first line sprint-stage-decisions (the PO sets the goal before What, ends refinement before How, gives the go-ahead before building, authorizes Test apart from approving the Increment, then decides close or return) is the umbrella stage-gates line plus the Sprint section of the stage-gates long file. Long file: no placeholder is recorded as a commitment while no Sprint Goal is set; the goal's exact text goes in the section 1.1 table; its wording is kept on the dated decision line as a record, not as a source; show the text to the PO only when the goal changed, direction is at issue, or they ask; after Test the PO decides to close or to return; a Developer's checks while building are not Sprint Test.

adds_to_target: What goes to the PO: whenever you are unsure, and in any case to set the Sprint Goal, select the items, say when refinement is over, give the go-ahead, decide at the end of each stage, renegotiate the acceptance criteria, decide whether new work enters the Sprint and renegotiate the scope, give formal acceptance when it is written, consent to outward actions such as a push, and cancel a Sprint whose goal can no longer be met.
note: The index of what the PO decides. Merged into ask-the-po with the design version (design-log#21); each decision still has its own line (sprint-goal, select-items, refinement, go-ahead, new-work-registered, acceptance-when-written, outward-needs-po, po-owns-commitments), so the index adds nothing to the list. Marked for the 27 sync with ask-the-po.

line: - **developer-elsewhere** With a Developer elsewhere the sprint log stays the record; talk directly, else take turns. Read details/handoff.md first.
note: Long file, without tool names: sessions that can talk (another session in the same tool, or a Developer forked from the Scrum Master's session) talk directly, a long review is a file and the message gives its path; otherwise one working copy and turns, the one with the turn commits only within the authorized scope and if permitted, writes what was done in the notes and says whose turn is next, the reviewer's findings reach the Developer as a file the PO passes on, which the Developer copies into the log, and the PO carries only the word that it is the other side's turn. 'These are examples, not rules.'
